paragraphs: Meporash bedibre rabbenu haari za"l beshaar taame hammitzot dap s" vezeh leshono: gam tzarik shetteda deap al pi shennitbaer leel shebbetok hasseuda im hu bechol yitatztzeb el libbo, ubiprat im hu beyachid al hachurban kannizkar beshem hazzohar, amenam bebirkat hammazon adderabba tzarik leharot simcha yetera belibbo, vehattaam ki inyan haakila hu bammalkut haelyona hannehenet meshuppa hattiperet, veal yede mah sheanachnu mekavvenim baakilatenu anachnu mamshikim lah hashshepa umazon, umimmah sheanachnu mamshikim lah hi mechalleqet venotenet mazon elenu, ulekak tzarik lebarek birkat hammazon beayin toba velo ketzare ayin veku' ad kan leshono, yeuyyan sham, al ken kol adam yizzaher lebarek birkat hammazon besimcha ubetub leb ubekavvana gedola, veim en lo kos beyado yihyu yadayv asurot zo al gab zo al hechazeh, veotzem enayv umebarek bekavvana ukemo shekkatub rabbenu za"l:

clarification.explanation: The Ari wrote that although during the meal itself, on a weekday, it is fitting to feel some sorrow over the Destruction, in Birkat HaMazon itself one must, on the contrary, show extra joy in the heart. The reason: the matter of eating belongs to the attribute of Malchut, which is nourished from the flow of Tiferet, and through the intention of our eating we draw down flow and sustenance to it, and from what it receives it distributes and gives to us; therefore one must bless Birkat HaMazon with a generous eye and not with a stingy eye. Therefore every person should be careful to bless Birkat HaMazon with joy, with a glad heart, and with great intention. And if he has no cup in hand, he should bind his hands one over the other on his chest, close his eyes, and bless with intention.
takeaways: Birkat HaMazon is recited with joy and a generous eye (unlike the sorrow appropriate during the meal itself)
Without a cup: hands clasped on the chest, eyes closed, with intention

paragraphs: Katab rabbenu harasha"sh za"l besiddur shello vezeh leshono qodem birkat hammazon yekavven lehakin atzmo leqayyem mitzvat aseh lebarek birkat hammazon beyira ubeahaba ubekavvana atzuma ubesimcha rabba ubetub lebab lehamshik shepa uberaka rabba umochin vechayyot umazon lemalkuta qaddisha daatzilut, umimmenna lanu ulekol haolamot haqqedoshim, veyaatzom enayv veyeesor yadayv zo al gab zo yemanit al hassemalit keyosheb lipne hammelek malko shel olam malkuta qaddisha daatzilut od katub sham yekavven shehu mukan leqayyem mitzvat aseh deorayeta lebarek achar hammazon shenneemar veakalta vesabaetta uberakta veku', v"y kavvanat hakana zo az yihyeh koach bekavvanato bibraka lehaalot mayin nuqbin ulehamshik arba mochin libchinat y"h veku' yeuyyan sham:

Ubesipri haqqatan mqbtzyl katabti nussach lomar qodem birkat hammazon: leshem yichud qadesha berik hu ushekinatah veku' hare anachnu baim leqayyem mitzvat aseh deorayeta lebarek birkat hammazon kakkatub battora veakalta vesabaetta uberakta et Adonai eloheka al haaretz hattoba asher natan lak letaqqen shoresh mitzva zo bemaqom elyon, vihi ratzon millepaneka Adonai elohenu velohe abotenu shettehe chashuba umequbbelet uretzuya lepaneka beraka rishona uberaka sheniyya uberaka shelishit asher nebarek atta al hammazon, vattitten lanu koach vikolet veezer vesiyyua lehaalot mayin nuqbin ulehamshik arbaa mochin leyisrael verachel, vegam tihyeh chashuba umequbbelet uretzuya lepaneka beraka rebiit asher nebarek atta vetitten lanu koach vikolet veezer vesiyyua lehaalot mayin nuqbin ulehamshik arbaa orot mochin leyaaqob verachel, veyaaleh lepaneka keillu kivvenu bekol hakkavvanot hareuyot lekavven bearba berakot ellu shel hammazon vayhi noam veku':

clarification.explanation: The Rashash wrote that before Birkat HaMazon one should intend to prepare himself to fulfill the positive commandment, to bless with awe, love, tremendous intention, joy, and a glad heart, in order to draw down flow and blessing and mochin and vitality and sustenance to the holy Malchut, and from her to us and to all the worlds; and he should close his eyes and bind his hands one over the other (right over left) as one sitting before the King. And our teacher, in his book, wrote a text of "Leshem Yichud" to say before the blessing, in which one requests that the first three blessings (which are from the Torah) and the fourth blessing be considered important and accepted before God, that he be granted the strength to draw down the mochin properly, and that it be accounted as though he had directed all the proper intentions in the four blessings.
takeaways: Before the blessing we prepare ourselves to bless with awe, love, joy, and intention
One recites "Leshem Yichud" so that the blessings be accepted and rise as though all the proper intentions had been directed

paragraphs: Arba berakot shel birkat hammazon dinam kitpillat shemoneh esreh, veen laanot bahem apillu qaddish uqedushsha ubareku veken lishol bebirkat hammazon mippene hayyira umippene hakkabod dino kitpillat shemoneh esreh, veim beto samuk lebet hakkeneset o hayu mitpallelim minyan betok beto veshama modim yarkin rosho letzad shehaqqahal mishtachavim, ubeshameu qaddish uqedushsha yishtoq veyishma kedin tepillat shemoneh esreh:

clarification.explanation: The four blessings of Birkat HaMazon have the law of the Amidah prayer: one may not respond to Kaddish, Kedushah, or Barchu during them, and one may not greet another, because of awe and honor. And if his house is adjacent to the synagogue, or a minyan was praying in his house, upon hearing "Modim" he should bow his head in the direction the congregation is bowing, and upon hearing Kaddish or Kedushah he should be silent and listen, as is the law during the Amidah.
takeaways: Birkat HaMazon is like the Amidah: one does not respond to Kaddish/Kedushah in it and does not greet others
Upon hearing Kaddish/Kedushah, one is silent and listens; upon "Modim," one bows the head

paragraphs: Tzarik lesheb bishat birkat hammazon, velo yebarek omed o mehallek im eno badderek, vegam lo yehe meseb shehu derek gaava ella yesheb beema, veyesh omerim degam beraka meen shalosh tzarik leomerah meyushshab, vetob lizzaher bekol habberakot:

clarification.explanation: One must sit during Birkat HaMazon, and should not bless while standing or walking (unless traveling), and should also not recline, as this is a manner of haughtiness; rather he should sit with awe. And some say that even the blessing Me'ein Shalosh (recited after cake, wine, or fruit) must be said while seated, and it is good to be careful about this in all blessings.
takeaways: Birkat HaMazon is recited seated and with awe, not standing and not reclining
It is good to recite even Me'ein Shalosh while seated as well

paragraphs: Asur lebarek vehu oseq bimlakto, apillu tashmish qal kegon menaggeb yadayv o lebush malbusho vekayyotze, upoh irenu sheyyesh chom harbeh bimot haqqayitz vederek haolam lehanip bikli sheqqorin mrvvch"h (menipa meale lulab) al happanim veal haggup, tzerikin lehizzaher shello yanipu beyadam bebirkat hammazon bikli zeh dezeh chashib eseq, ki birkat hammazon utepillat haamida dinam shaveh beinyanim elleh veen hepresh benehem ki im bedabar zeh shehattepilla meummad ubirkat hammazon meyushshab, vehen baavonotenu harabbim rabbim meamme haaretz mezalzelim bebirkat hammazon lebarek otah bimhirut meod, veyesh oseq beezeh eseq beet habberaka gam romez beenayv qoretz bispatayv molel beetzbeotayv vekayyotze bazeh, vetzarik lehokicham al zot bemoser hassekel velashshomeim yinam vaalehem tabo birkat tob:

clarification.explanation: It is forbidden to bless Birkat HaMazon while engaged in work, even a light activity such as drying the hands or putting on a garment. And in a place where it is customary to fan oneself on the face and body due to heat, one must be careful not to fan oneself during the blessing, since this is considered an activity — for Birkat HaMazon and the Amidah prayer are equal in these matters, and the only difference between them is that prayer is said standing and Birkat HaMazon seated. Many are lax regarding Birkat HaMazon and bless it very quickly, or engage in activity during the blessing and gesture with their eyes and fingers, and one should rebuke them about this.
takeaways: One does not bless while engaged in an activity, even a light one (drying hands, fanning oneself)
Birkat HaMazon is equal to the Amidah, and one should not be lax or hurry through it

paragraphs: Nohagim lehasir hassakkin min hashshulchan bishat birkat hammazon, vehamdaqdeqim mesirim kol keli barzel kegon hammazleg vehammisparayim shel neyarot, vekatebu acharonim za"l deen lehaqpid al kol hannizkar leel beshabbat veyom tob ubeshaar rucha haqqodesh dap y"b ita beshem rabbenu haari"y za"l mi shehu mishshoresh qayin tzarik lehizzaher lehasir hassakkin legamre beet birkat hammazon velo yaspiq lekassoto bilbad yeuyyan sham, ulekak kol adam tzarik lehizzaher bah deen ittanu yodea hashsharashim, veken anachnu nohagim lahasiro gam beshabbat veyom tob:

clarification.explanation: It is customary to remove the knife from the table during Birkat HaMazon, and the more meticulous remove every iron implement (fork, scissors). The Acharonim wrote that one need not be strict about this on Shabbat and Yom Tov, but it is brought in the name of the Ari that one who is of the root of Kayin must remove the knife entirely during the blessing, and it is not enough merely to cover it; therefore every person must be careful about this, since we do not know our roots — and so our teacher is accustomed to remove it even on Shabbat and Yom Tov as well.
takeaways: One removes a knife (and the meticulous remove iron implements) during Birkat HaMazon
It is customary to remove it even on Shabbat and Yom Tov, since one's root is unknown

paragraphs: Bebirkat hammazon yashmia leazenayv mah shemmotzi bispatayv, vp al gab demera"n za"l sebira lah im lo hishmia leazenayv yatza bediabad, tzarik lehachmir deim yesh lo od pat yachzor veyokal vibarek karauy kede shello yikkanes bispeq bittul mitzvat aseh min hattora, mishshum deyesh omerim im lo hishmia leazenayv lo yatza veayyen chesed leabraham siman qp"h ot ':

clarification.explanation: During Birkat HaMazon one should make audible to his own ears what he utters with his lips. And although Maran holds that after the fact one has fulfilled the obligation even without making it audible to his ears, one should be stringent: if he has more bread, he should go back and eat and bless properly, so as not to enter into a doubt regarding the nullification of a positive Torah commandment, since some say that if he did not make it audible to his ears he has not fulfilled his obligation.
takeaways: One makes Birkat HaMazon audible to his own ears
If he did not make it audible and has more bread: he should eat and bless again, out of doubt regarding a Torah obligation

paragraphs: Yesh omerim im akal velo shata mayim im hu taeb lishtot eno chayyab lebarek birkat hammazon min hattora ella raq midderabbanan, lepikak im akal velo shata mayim vehu taeb lishtot yishtaddel bekol kocho lehamtzi mayim ulehamtin ad sheyyabiu lo mayim veyishteh kede sheyyebarek birkat hammazon min hattora veim lo nimtza lo mayim lishtot chayyab bebirkat hammazon midderabbanan:

clarification.explanation: Some say that one who ate bread and did not drink water, if he is thirsty, is not obligated in Birkat HaMazon from the Torah but only rabbinically. Therefore one who ate and did not drink and is thirsty should make every effort to obtain water and wait until it is brought to him and drink, so as to bless Birkat HaMazon by Torah law. And if no water is found for him, he is obligated in Birkat HaMazon rabbinically.
takeaways: One who ate and is thirsty but did not drink: according to this view, obligated only rabbinically
He should make an effort to drink water in order to become obligated by Torah law

paragraphs: Im akal pat velo shata mayim mishshum deeno taeb lishtot, o sheshshata mayim dibkol zeh hu chayyab bebirkat hammazon min hattora, venistappeq aach"k im berak birkat hammazon o lav, tzarik lebarek shelosha berakot mippene shehem min hattora usepeqa lechumera, abal hattob vehammetib shehi midderabbanan lo mebarek missapeq. v"g deikka disbira lehu sheyyebarek gam zo, ha qayma lan sapeq berakot lehaqel, vehu haddin im taa beemtza birkat hammazon veeno yodea hekan taa o shennitnamnem veeno yodea beezo beraka omed dechozer larosh mishshum sepeq tora, veraq bibraka rebiit im hu mistappeq bah lo yebarek, mihu im lo akal de sebia deeno chayyab min hattora bebirkat hammazon, o akal kede sebia ak haya tzame velo shata degam ken eno chayyab bebirkat hammazon min hattora, hare zeh lo yachazor lebarek min hassapeq apillu shelosha berakot kevan deeno chayyab lebarek ella midderabbanan, veim epshar lo leekol mechadash ulebarek shappir dame.

Veken haokel pat habbaa bekisanin venistappeq im berak meen shalosh o lav, veken im sapeq lo im akal kazzayit pat o pachot veken ishsha sheakela pat veshiba venistappeqa im beraka birkat hammazon o lav, im epshar leekol mechadash ulebarek o latzet bibraka shel acherim mah tob, veim lav lo yebareku missapeq:

clarification.explanation: One who ate bread (and was not thirsty, or drank water), and is thus obligated in Birkat HaMazon from the Torah, and becomes uncertain whether he blessed, must recite the first three blessings, which are from the Torah and a doubt regarding them is treated stringently — but should not bless "HaTov VeHaMeitiv" (the fourth, rabbinic blessing) out of doubt. Likewise, if he erred in the middle and does not know where, or dozed off, he returns to the beginning (out of Torah doubt), and only regarding the fourth blessing, if in doubt, he does not go back. But one who is obligated only rabbinically (did not eat enough to be satiated, or was satiated but thirsty and did not drink) does not go back to bless even the three blessings out of doubt; and if it is possible for him to eat anew and bless, all the better. Likewise one who eats pat haba'ah bekisnin and is in doubt about Me'ein Shalosh, or is in doubt whether he ate a kezayit, or a woman who ate and was satiated and is uncertain — if it is possible to eat again or to fulfill the obligation through others' blessing, all the better; and if not, they should not bless out of doubt.
takeaways: Obligated from the Torah and in doubt: he blesses the three [Torah] blessings, but not "HaTov VeHaMeitiv"
Obligated only rabbinically and in doubt: he does not go back; if possible he should eat again or hear it from others

paragraphs: "p sheameru deshalosh berakot tzarik al hassapeq gam ken, hinneh im nizdammen sheakal kede sebia uberak birkat hammazon, veachar shaa qetanna chazar veakal kazzayit bilbad vesaba mimmennu mippene ki hayeta akilato hashsheniyya semuka laakila harishona, kegon seuda shelishit shel shabbat veakal achareha samuk lah seuda rebiit, nistappequ bedabar zeh happoseqim im akila sheniyya nechshebet sebia min hattora kevan debeemet saba atta bikzayit zeh, o dilma en zo sebia mippene shehishbia baa mikkoach akila harishona hassemuka lah shekkebar berak aleha birkat hammazon ulekak eno mechuyyab bashsheniyya bebirkat hammazon min hattora, veken hu haddin im akal kazzayit sheen bo kede sebia meatzmo veraq mechamat sheakal maakalim acherim immo naasa sabea im chayyab bazeh min hattora, vela ippeshatu hane sepeqe heteb lepikak im era lo behane obede sapeq bebirkat hammazon sheeno yodea im berak im lav lo yachazor lebarek apillu shelosha berakot, ella yishma birkat hammazon meacherim shemmebarekim al akilatam karauy veyitkavven latzet yede choba veyitkonenu gam hem lehotzio yede choba, veayyen "ara deyisrael" maareket habbe"t ot y" uperi megadim siman qp"d seip qatan ch' v"chesed laalapim" qp"d mechuddash g' veod acharonim:

clarification.explanation: Although we said that in cases of doubt one blesses three blessings, if one ate enough to be satiated and blessed, and a short while later ate only a kezayit and was satiated by it (because his second eating was close to the first, such as the third Shabbat meal followed closely by a fourth meal), the poskim were in doubt whether this satiation obligates from the Torah (since he is indeed satiated now) or not (since the satiation stems from the force of the first eating, over which he already blessed). Likewise if he ate a kezayit that by itself is not enough for satiation, and became satiated only in combination with other foods. Since these doubts were not clearly resolved, if such a doubt occurs to him in Birkat HaMazon, he should not go back and bless even the three blessings, but rather listen to Birkat HaMazon from others and intend to fulfill his obligation, and they should intend to discharge his obligation.
takeaways: Being satiated from a kezayit close to a prior meal, or being satiated only in combination with other foods: the Torah obligation is in doubt
In doubt in such cases: do not go back, but rather listen to others and intend to fulfill the obligation

paragraphs: Nashim chayyabot bebirkat hammazon, vehen baaon atta rabbot banot okelot belo beraka mechamat chesron yedia vaatidot hen vaabihen ubalehen litten et haddin, verauy lekol adam lelammed et bitto binureha bet abiha nosach birkat hannehenin ubirkat hammazon lepachot nosach haqqatzar hakkatub basseparim, veim lo lemidda bebet abiha chayyab balah lelamedah vekannizkar kol zeh bechesed laalapim, vaana abeda poh irenu y" hidpasti nosach haqqatzar shel birkat hammazon shebbo mazkirin meen hamora beshabbat veyom tob verosh chodesh, lechelqo lannashim bechinnam, verabot banot baot veloqechot nosach zeh hannidpas mibbetenu, vegam im nussach hannizkar hidpasti nussach qatzar beyoter leotam hammitatztzelim beyoter veen yodeim lilmod ashshurit dilpachot yomru zeh bimqom birkat hammazon vehu berik rachamana maran malka dealema mareh dehay pitta berik rachamana dezan lekulla, venussach qatzar zeh yekolim lelammedo beal peh achar hergelam bo:

clarification.explanation: Women are obligated in Birkat HaMazon. And because of our sins, many of them eat without a blessing due to lack of knowledge — and they, their father, and their husbands are destined to give an accounting for this. Therefore it is fitting for every person to teach his daughter, in her youth while still in her father's house, the text of the blessings on enjoyment and Birkat HaMazon — at least the short text found in the books; and if her father did not teach her, her husband is obligated to teach her (Chesed La'alafim). And the Ben Ish Chai relates that he printed in his city the short text of Birkat HaMazon (which mentions the special occasion on Shabbat, Yom Tov, and Rosh Chodesh) to distribute to women free of charge, and many come and take it; and he also printed an even shorter text for those who do not know how to read the Ashurit script — that they should at least say, in place of Birkat HaMazon: "Berikh Rachamana Maran Malka De'alma Marei Dehai Pita, Berikh Rachamana Dezan Lechulla," a text that can be learned by heart.
takeaways: Women are obligated in Birkat HaMazon; it is fitting to teach every daughter in her youth, and if not — the husband is obligated to teach her.
At least the short text; and one who cannot read should say by heart: "Berikh Rachamana Maran Malka De'alma Marei Dehai Pita, Berikh Rachamana Dezan Lechulla."

paragraphs: Yesh bene adam sheddarkam leekol leat leat veen okelim shiur kazzayit shalem shehu tisha drh"m betok akilat peras, shehu shiur akilat shalosh betzim shehem n"d drh"m, velaken tzarik lehazhiram meod bedabar zeh shello lishhot baakilat kazzayit shiur akilat peras, veachar sheyyoklu kazzayit karauy az yesayyemu akilatam kirtzonam leekol leat leat, yaan ki rabbim min happoseqim za"l disbira lehu: im shaha baakilat kazzayit shehu shiur hachiyyub yoter mikkede akilat peras en mebarek birkat hammazon velo shum beraka acharona, vesabera zo iqqar "p deyesh choleqin, ubiprat deqayma lan sapeq berakot lehaqel veayyen zekor leabraham cheleq g' beresh qunteres acharon, veniktob od beinyan zeh leqamman b"h beparasha acheret:

clarification.explanation: There are people who eat slowly and do not eat a full kezayit (nine dirhams) within "the time it takes to eat a peras" (the measure of eating three eggs, fifty-four dirhams). One must warn them strongly not to delay eating the kezayit beyond the time it takes to eat a peras, and after eating a proper kezayit they may finish eating slowly as they wish. This is because many poskim hold that if one delayed eating the kezayit (the measure of obligation) beyond the time it takes to eat a peras, he does not bless Birkat HaMazon or any after-blessing at all, and this view is primary — particularly since a doubt regarding blessings is treated leniently.
takeaways: One must eat a kezayit of bread within "the time it takes to eat a peras" (the time of three eggs)
If he delayed longer: he does not recite an after-blessing; after the kezayit he may continue slowly

paragraphs: Im akal veheqi vehu mesuppaq im nishar bemeayv kazzayit mimmah sheakal, hare zeh niknas bebet hassapeq velo yebarek birkat hammazon ella ad sheyyokal od im epshar lo leekol, veim lo epshar lo yishma beraka meacherim veyitkavven latzet yede choba, veim gam zeh lo epshar yebarek birkat hammazon beli shem umalkut raq yeharher shem umalkut velo yotzi mippiv, vedin zeh lav davqa bebirkat hammazon ella yeshno gam beokel o shoteh yayin veheqi dedina haki kaasher katabnu veayyen acharonim:

clarification.explanation: One who ate and vomited, and is uncertain whether a kezayit of what he ate remained in his stomach, enters a state of doubt and should not bless Birkat HaMazon unless he eats more (if possible). And if that is not possible, he should listen to the blessing from others and intend to fulfill his obligation. And if that too is not possible, he should bless Birkat HaMazon without mentioning God's name and sovereignty, contemplating the name and sovereignty in his heart. This law applies also to one who eats or drinks wine and then vomits.
takeaways: Vomited and it is in doubt whether a kezayit remained: he should not bless unless he eats again
If that is not possible: he should listen to others, and as a last resort bless without God's name and sovereignty, contemplating them instead

paragraphs: Bibraka rishona yatchil kak "baruk atta Adonai elohenu melek haolam hael hazzan otanu veet haolam kullo betubo veku'". veken hu besiddur rabbenu harasha"sh za"l degaras "hael veku'" ukesheomer poteach et yadeka yekavven rashe tebot poteach et yadeka begematreya yhdvnh"y vikavven sope tebot cht"k vb"t b"sh saa"l begematreya yhdvnh"y, ubetebat "umasbia" yekavven shehu begematreya cht"k, ukesheomer lekol chay ratzon yekavven sheyyimmashek shepa umazon uberaka rabba lekol haolamot ukeshechotem beraka rishona beshabbat yosip lekavven behazkarat hashshem shel habberaka bhvy"h demilluy yvdy"n shehu yu"d h"y vay"v h"y, veod yekavven bemilluy hayyo"d kazeh yo"d va"v dale"t vekannizkar besiddur rabbenu harasha"sh za"l:

clarification.explanation: In the first blessing one begins "Blessed are You, Lord our God, King of the universe, who nourishes us and the entire world in His goodness," and so reads the Rashash, "HaEl," etc. When he says "Poteach et Yadecha," he should intend, in the initial letters (Poteach Et Yadecha), the holy name Yud-Kei-Vav-Kei by numerical value, and likewise in the final letters (Chet-Tav-Kaf), by the At-Bash cipher, the same name Yud-Kei-Vav-Kei; and in the word "UMasbi'a" he should intend that it equals numerically Chet-Tav-Kaf. And when he says "LeChol Chai Ratzon," he should intend to draw down flow, sustenance, and abundant blessing to all the worlds. And in concluding the blessing on Shabbat he should add the intention of the name Yud-Kei-Vav-Kei in the spelling of the Yudin (Yud-Vav-Dalet Heh-Yud Vav-Yud-Vav Heh-Yud), and further intend the spelling of the Yud itself (Yud-Vav-Dalet).
takeaways: First blessing: "who nourishes us and the entire world in His goodness"
In "Poteach et Yadecha" one intends, in both the initial and final letters, the name Yud-Kei-Vav-Kei, and in "UMasbi'a" one intends the numerical value Chet-Tav-Kaf
On Shabbat one adds the intention of the name Yud-Kei-Vav-Kei in the spelling of the Yudin and in the spelling of the Yud

paragraphs: Bibraka sheniyya yatchil nodeh leka veku', ubassiddurim vesimchat haregel katub veal chayyim umazon sheatta zan umeparnes otanu, ak bechesed laalapim katab kak veal chayyim shechonantanu veal hammazon sheatta zan veku' venireh garesa zo yoter nekona, veyomar al hakkol belo va"v, ubachatima dibraka sheniyya yosip beshabbat lekavven behazkarat hashshem bhvy"h demilluy s"g kazeh yo"d h"y va"v h"y, veod yekavven bemilluy h"y yu"d vekannizkar besiddur harasha"sh za"l:

clarification.explanation: In the second blessing of Birkat HaMazon one begins "Nodeh Lecha." In the siddurim and in the book Simchat HaRegel it is written "Ve'al Chayim UMazon She'Atah Zan UMefarnes Otanu," but in Chesed La'alafim the text is "Ve'al Chayim SheChonantanu Ve'al HaMazon She'Atah Zan," etc., and this version appears more correct; and he should say "Al HaKol" without the vav. And in concluding the second blessing he should add, on Shabbat, the intention of mentioning God's name — the Tetragrammaton — in the filling of Samech-Gimel (Yud-Vav-Dalet, Heh-Yud, Vav-Aleph-Vav, Heh-Yud), and further intend the filling "Heh-Yud Yud," as brought in the siddur of the Rashash, zal.
takeaways: The precise text of the second blessing: "Ve'al Chayim SheChonantanu Ve'al HaMazon She'Atah Zan," and "Al HaKol" without the vav.
On Shabbat, at the conclusion — intention of the name Yud-Kei-Vav-Kei in the filling of Samech-Gimel (per the siddur of the Rashash).

paragraphs: Beraka shelishit yatchil rachem Adonai elohenu veku', vegam yizzaher lomar reenu zunenu, velo kemo shekkatub roenu zunenu, gam yomar vena al tatzrikenu Adonai elohenu lide mattenot basar vadam veku', yehi ratzon shello nebosh veku', uberatza vehachlitzenu yomar nishbot bo venanucha bo venitannag bo, veyomar vegam sheakalnu veshatinu velo yomar veap, vaapillu beshabbat tzarik lomar qodem hachatima shel habberaka vetibneh yerushalayim ir haqqodesh bimhera beyamenu baruk atta Adonai boneh yerushalayim, v"g sheyyesh goresin boneh berachamayv, sheb veal taaseh adip velo yomar berachamayv vknz' baacharonim, ubachatimat beraka zo beshabbat yosip lekavven beshem shel hachatima bemilluy alpin shehu yo"d he" va"v he" veod yekavven bemilluy vay"v yu"d vay"v vekannizkar besiddur rabbenu harasha"sh za"l, veachar chatima zo deboneh yerushalayim yaaneh amen achar birkat atzmo mippene shehu siyyum berakot deorayeta, ki beraka rebiit hi derabbanan:

clarification.explanation: In the third blessing one begins "Rachem Hashem Elokeinu," and says "Re'enu Zunenu" (not "Ro'einu"), "VeNa Al Tatzricheinu Hashem Elokeinu Lidei Matnot Basar VaDam," and on Shabbat "Retzeh VeHachalitzeinu... Nishbot Bo VeNanuach Bo VeNit'anag Bo," "VeGam She'achalnu VeShatinu" (not "Ve'af"). Even on Shabbat, one says before the conclusion "VeTivneh Yerushalayim Ir HaKodesh Bimheirah VeYameinu, Baruch Atah Hashem Boneh Yerushalayim," and should not say "Boneh BeRachamav" (it is better to refrain than to add). On Shabbat one adds, at the conclusion, the intention of the name Yud-Kei-Vav-Kei in the filling of the Alfin. And after the conclusion "Boneh Yerushalayim," one answers "Amen" after his own blessing, since it is the conclusion of the blessings that are from the Torah (the fourth blessing being rabbinic).
takeaways: Third blessing: precise wording, and on Shabbat "Retzeh VeHachalitzeinu" before "Boneh Yerushalayim"
One answers "Amen" after "Boneh Yerushalayim," since it is the conclusion of the Torah blessings

paragraphs: Beraka rebiit yekavven bah shehu mukan leqayyem mitzva derabbanan lebarek beraka derabbanan v"y kavvanat hakana zo az yihyeh koach bekavvanato bibraka zo lehaalot mayin nuqbin ulehamshik arba orot mochin libchinat yaaqob verachel, vekannizkar besiddur rabbenu harasha"sh za"l, ukeshemmatchil bibraka zo beshabbat yosip lekavven beshem shel habberaka bhvy"h demilluy hhy"n shehu yu"d h"h va"v h"h veod yekavven bemilluy h"y yu"d vekannizkar sham, venussach haamitti lomar hu hetib lanu hu metib lanu hu yetib lanu, hu gemalanu hu gomelenu hu yigmelenu, vezeh hannosach hu al derek haya hoveh veyihyeh velo yomar hannussach shehu mesuddar al derek melek melek yimlok veken hu besiddur rabbenu harasha"sh za"l, vesham timtza kavvanot bekol teba veteba shel beraka zo mah sheen ken bishar berakot umizzeh tabin maalat beraka zo, veim mechamat hammehirut mechasser achat mehen o mablia hare zeh meabbed toba harbeh, vehannizhar tabo alayv birkat tob:

clarification.explanation: In the fourth blessing one should intend that he is prepared to fulfill a rabbinic positive commandment by reciting a rabbinic blessing, and through this preparatory intention there will be power in his intention in this blessing to raise up mayin nukvin and to draw down four lights of mochin to the aspect of "Yaakov and Rachel" (as explained in the siddur of the Rashash). And when he begins this blessing on Shabbat, he should add the intention of the name Yud-Kei-Vav-Kei in the blessing, in the filling of the Heh-Heh's — that is, Yud-Vav-Dalet Heh-Heh Vav-Alef-Vav Heh-Heh — and should further intend an additional filling: Heh-Yud Yud. And the correct text to say is: "Hu Heitiv Lanu, Hu Meitiv Lanu, Hu Yeitiv Lanu; Hu Gemalanu, Hu Gomleinu, Hu Yigmeleinu" — this text is built on the pattern of "was, is, and will be," and one should not say the text built on the pattern "King, King, will reign," as it appears in the siddur of the Rashash. And there, intentions are explained for every single word of this blessing, unlike the other blessings — from which one may understand its special elevated quality. And one who, out of haste, omits one of these intentions, or slurs over the text instead of saying it properly, loses much good; and one who is careful about this shall have the blessing of good come upon him.
takeaways: In the fourth blessing one should intend that it fulfills a rabbinic positive commandment.
On Shabbat one adds intention of the name Yud-Kei-Vav-Kei in two fillings: the filling of the Heh-Heh's (Yud-Vav-Dalet Heh-Heh Vav-Alef-Vav Heh-Heh) and the filling Heh-Yud Yud.
The correct text: "Hu Heitiv Lanu Hu Meitiv Lanu Hu Yeitiv Lanu, Hu Gemalanu Hu Gomleinu Hu Yigmeleinu" — not the text "King, King, will reign."
One who rushes and omits or slurs part of the text or the intention loses much good; one should take care to say it in full.

paragraphs: Kesheomer hambarek harachaman az kol hayyosheb chayyab laanot amen achar kol baqqasha ubaqqasha deharachaman kemo shekkatab "chesed laalapim" rt"v ot d', v"g deen asur lehapsiq bitchinnot ellu deharachaman mikkol maqom asur lehapsiq besichat chol, vehammebarek al hakkos chal alayv hachiyyub tepe shello yapsiq ben birkat hammazon lebirkat bore peri haggapen dekos, veayyen mishbetzot zahab siman qp"t umayim hachayyim siman Adonai yeuyyan sham veod acharonim, ukesheomer harachaman yebarek kol echad veechad mimmennu, im yesh akku"m yoshebim sham yomar kol echad veechad mimmennu bene berit, ukesheomer harachaman hu yitta torato veku' yosip lomar veyihyu kol maasenu leshem shamayim vehaoreach yizzaher lebarek et baal habbayit ki zo hi taqqanat chaza"l vekol hambarek mitbarek, veim habbaal habbayit eno oseh hasseuda laorechim bebeto yomar haoreach hu yebarek et baal hasseuda hazzot, veim baale habbayit hem rabbim shehem achi veshuttape bisuda zo yomar yebarek et baale hasseuda hazzot veyomar bebanim sheyyichyu ubinkasim sheyyirbu veayyen kap hachayyim, ubisudat chatan yebarek hechatan vehakkalla, ubisudat mila yebarek hayyeled hannimmol keshem veku' gam kesheomer harachaman hu yeparnesennu bekabod velo bebizzuy veku' lo yomar behetter velo beissur, deha vadday hqb"h yeparnesennu behetter velo beissur veek yomar ken bederek baqqasha lebaqqesh mehashshem yitbarek al dabar zeh, veken name yizzaher bebaqqasha shel happarnasa sheomerim berosh hashshana ubeyom hakkippurim:

clarification.explanation: When the one blessing says "HaRachaman," all those seated are obligated to answer "Amen" after every petition. Although it is not forbidden to interrupt for these petitions of "HaRachaman," it is forbidden to interrupt them with mundane conversation, and one who blesses over a cup must be careful not to interrupt between Birkat HaMazon and the blessing "Borei Peri HaGafen." In "HaRachaman Hu Yevarech Kol Echad Ve'Echad Mimenu," if gentiles are present, he should say "each and every one of us, members of the covenant." The guest should be careful to bless the host, since this is an enactment of the Sages, and whoever blesses is blessed, using the appropriate wording for the occasion (the master of the meal, the groom and bride, the child who was circumcised). And in "HaRachaman Hu Yefarnesenu BeKavod," he should not say "BeHeter VeLo Be'Isur," since it is not fitting to request, as a matter of petition, something that God will certainly do in any case.
takeaways: One answers "Amen" after every "HaRachaman"; the guest blesses the host
One does not interrupt with mundane conversation, and does not say "BeHeter VeLo Be'Isur"

paragraphs: Bearba seudot shabbat veken beyom tob vechol hammoed verosh chodesh omerim migdol bv"v, vekatab bechesed lealpayim beshem harab rabbi david padaro za"l sheggam bisudat mila rauy lomar miggadol beva"v al pi hassod yeuyyan sham, ubeseper keter malkut ketibat yad ita sheggam bisudat purim yomar miggadol beva"v bishbil otah heara hammitgalet bayyom hahu shehi temidit kol hayyom kullo, ubesiyyum hakkol yomar pasuq oseh shalom bimromayv veku', vikavven berashe tebot oseh bimromayv lhvy"h shel "b dyvdy"n, vekannizkar bedibre rabbenu haari"y za"l beshaar hammitzvot parashat eqeb:

clarification.explanation: At the four meals of Shabbat — and likewise on Yom Tov, Chol HaMo'ed, and Rosh Chodesh — one says "Magdol" with a vav (not "Magdil"). And Chesed La'alafim wrote in the name of Rabbi David Pardo, zal, that at a circumcision meal as well it is fitting to say "Magdol" with a vav, according to the esoteric tradition; and in the handwritten book Keter Malchut it is stated that at a Purim meal as well one should say "Magdol" with a vav, on account of that illumination revealed on that day, which is constant throughout the entire day. And at the very end one says the verse "Oseh Shalom Bimromav," etc., intending in the initial letters "Oseh Bimromav" the name Yud-Kei-Vav-Kei of the seventy-two-name expansion with Yudin — as brought in the words of our teacher the Ari, zal, in Sha'ar HaMitzvot, Parashat Eikev.
takeaways: On Shabbat, Yom Tov, Chol HaMo'ed, Rosh Chodesh — and also at a circumcision and at Purim (according to the esoteric tradition) — one says "Magdol" with a vav.
At the conclusion one says "Oseh Shalom Bimromav" and intends in the initial letters "Oseh Bimromav" the name of the seventy-two-name expansion with Yudin.

paragraphs: Beshabbat omer bibraka shelishit retzeh vehachalitzenu, uperush hechlitzanu hu rotzeh lemor "zarezenu", ubeyom tob vechol hammoed verosh chodesh omer kan yaaleh veyabo veeno mazkir shabbat beyaaleh veyabo, veim taa velo hizkir shel shabbat bisudat hallayla o seuda harishona shel hayyom, im nizkar kesheamar baruk atta Adonai qodem sheamar boneh yerushalayim yesayyem lammedeni chuqqeka veyazkir retzeh vehachalitzenu, veim nizkar achar sheamar boneh yerushalayim qodem shehitchil beraka rebiit shel hattob vehammetib omer sham nosach zeh baruk atta Adonai elohenu melek haolam shennatan shabbatot limnucha leammo yisrael beahaba leot velibrit baruk atta Adonai meqaddesh hashshabbat, veim eno yodea nosach beraka zo yachzor lerosh birkat hammazon day sheyyazkir meen hamora meachar sheeno yodea letaqqen hachissaron, ella deim yada lomar hahatchala vehassiyyum saggi ap sheeno yodea hannussach kullo karauy, veim chal yom tob beshabbat vehutzrak lomar nussach zeh az yomar oto kak baruk atta Adonai elohenu melek haolam shennatan shabbatot limnucha leammo yisrael beahaba leot velibrit veyamim tobim lesason ulesimcha et yom chag peloni hazzeh baruk atta Adonai meqaddesh hashshabbat veyisrael vehazzemannim, veha desaggi behak beraka, davqa keshezzakar qodem shehitchil hattob vehammetib, abal im lo nizkar ad shehitchil birkat hattob vehammetib apillu lo amar adayin ella raq tebat baruk chozer lerosh birkat hammazon:

Veim taa bisuda shelishit shel shabbat yesh pelugta deyesh omerim chozer kedin seuda rishona usheniyya veyesh omerim deeno chozer, v"g deshurat haddin mechayyebet desapeq berakot lehaqel veeno chozer, mikkol maqom kevan dp"y hassod qayma lan en hepresh bechiyyuba ben seuda shelishit leben shette seudot deshavim hem bechiyyub, lekak tzarik lehorot gam bisuda shelishit chozer, mihu bisuda acheret shessoed beyom achar seuda deshacharit shebberek bah hammotzi ubirkat hammazon kulle alema modo deim taa bah eno chozer, veayyen birke yosep umachaziq beraka veiqqere hd"t siman y"g ot y"d:

clarification.explanation: On Shabbat one says in the third blessing "Retzeh VeHachalitzeinu" ("HeChelitzanu" meaning "strengthen us"). On Yom Tov, Chol HaMo'ed, and Rosh Chodesh one says there "Ya'aleh VeYavo" (without mentioning Shabbat). And if he erred and did not mention Shabbat at the evening meal or the first meal of the day: if he remembers after saying "Baruch Atah Hashem" but before "Boneh Yerushalayim," he concludes "Lamdeini Chukecha" and says "Retzeh VeHachalitzeinu"; and if he remembers after "Boneh Yerushalayim" but before the fourth blessing, he says the text "Baruch... She'natan Shabbatot Limnuchah... Baruch Atah Hashem Mekadesh HaShabbat" (and if Yom Tov falls on Shabbat he adds also "VeYamim Tovim LeSasson ULeSimchah" and mentions the holiday); and if he does not know this text, he returns to the beginning of Birkat HaMazon (it being sufficient to mention the essential opening and closing if he is not fluent in the entire text). And if he has already begun the blessing of "HaTov VeHaMeitiv" (even only the word "Baruch"), he returns to the beginning. And if he erred at the third meal of Shabbat — there is a dispute: some say he returns as in the law of the first two meals, and some say he does not return (since, strictly speaking, a doubt regarding blessings is treated leniently). Yet we rule that he should return even at the third meal, since according to the esoteric tradition there is no difference in obligation between the third meal and the other two — they are equal in obligation. But if he erred at an additional meal eaten that day, after the morning meal at which he already blessed "HaMotzi" and Birkat HaMazon — all agree that he does not return.
takeaways: On Shabbat one says "Retzeh VeHachalitzeinu," and on Yom Tov/Chol HaMo'ed/Rosh Chodesh "Ya'aleh VeYavo," without mentioning Shabbat.

One who forgot to mention Shabbat has a precise order of correction depending on the stage at which he remembers, up to returning to the beginning of Birkat HaMazon if he has already begun the fourth blessing.

Erred at the third meal — the custom is to be stringent and return, even though strictly speaking some are lenient, on account of the kabbalistic teaching that the three meals are equal in obligation.
At an additional meal on that day which is not one of the three primary meals — all agree that he does not return even if he erred.

paragraphs: Im taa beyom tob "g dekatebu happoseqim dechozer kedin taa beshabbat veken katab mera"n za"l, mikkol maqom kevan deyesh omerim deen lachazor beyom tob qayma lan sapeq berakot lehaqel veeno chozer beyom tob, chutz millel ' depesach velel ' desukkot, veayyen chesed laalapim siman qp"t umah shekkatab sham beshem mosheh yedabber siman ' yeuyyan sham:

clarification.explanation: If one erred and did not mention Yom Tov, although the poskim (and Maran as well) wrote that he returns as in the law of Shabbat, nevertheless, since some say that one does not return on Yom Tov, we follow the rule that a doubt regarding blessings is treated leniently, and he does not return on Yom Tov — except on the first night of Pesach and the first night of Sukkot (when there is an obligation to eat bread, and therefore he does return).
takeaways: Erred on Yom Tov: he does not return (a doubt regarding blessings is treated leniently)
Except on the first night of Pesach and Sukkot, when he does return

paragraphs: Haya okel veyatza shabbat mazkir shel shabbat bebirkat hammazon deazelinan batar hatchalat hasseuda v"g deyesh omerim batar hashta azelinan la qayma lan haki, veken hamminhag pashut lehazkir shel shabbat, umihu yedalleg tebat hazzeh, veim taa velo hizkir eno chozer, vehu haddin leyom tob deazelinan name batar hatchalat hasseuda, abal berosh chodesh vachanukka "g degam bazeh ikka pelugta morinan bahem dela yazkir, veim hitpallel arbit beemtza hasseuda apillu beshabbat eno mazkir:

Veha deamerinan beshel shabbat deim nimsheka seuda mazkir, mikkol maqom im nitakkel hammazon sheakal beshabbat eno mazkir, veim nizdammen rosh chodesh bemotzae shabbat eno mazkir ella shel shabbat dehave tarte desateran, ubibraka acharona shemmebarek al kos shel birkat hammazon eno mazkir shel shabbat, veken im bebet hechatan nimsheka hasseuda ad lel shemini eno mebarek shiba berakot al hakkos shel birkat hammazon vekannizkar bechesed laalapim siman qp"t ot z':

clarification.explanation: One who was eating and Shabbat departed in the middle of his meal mentions Shabbat in Birkat HaMazon, since we follow the beginning of the meal; and although some say we follow the present moment, the halachah is not so, and the widespread custom is to mention Shabbat — except that he omits the word "HaZeh." And if he erred and did not mention it, he does not return. The same applies to Yom Tov (we follow the beginning of the meal). But regarding Rosh Chodesh and Chanukah — although there is a dispute about these as well — we instruct that he should not mention them. And if he prayed the evening service in the middle of the meal, even on Shabbat, he does not mention it. And what we said, that on Shabbat, if the meal continued, he mentions it — that applies specifically if the food he ate on Shabbat has not yet been digested; but if it has been digested, he does not mention it. And if Rosh Chodesh falls on Motza'ei Shabbat, he mentions only Shabbat, since these are two contradictory matters. And in the final blessing recited over the cup of Birkat HaMazon, he does not mention Shabbat; and likewise, if at the groom's house the meal continued until the eighth night, he does not recite the Sheva Berachot over the cup of Birkat HaMazon (Chesed La'alafim).
takeaways: Shabbat/Yom Tov departed during the meal — he mentions it (following the beginning of the meal), but omits "HaZeh"; if he erred, he does not return.
Rosh Chodesh and Chanukah — one does not mention them; if he prayed the evening service in the middle, he does not mention it even on Shabbat.
If the food has been digested — he does not mention it; Rosh Chodesh on Motza'ei Shabbat — only Shabbat is mentioned; on the cup of Birkat HaMazon one does not mention Shabbat or Sheva Berachot.
